page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-8-lssd is a memory-optimized server instance from the c4 family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 2.3 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture. This configuration includes 4 physical cores with hyper-threading, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 62.0 GB of RAM, yielding 7.75 GB of memory per core, and includes a bundled 402 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed local storage.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1899.0 and a top-tier text processing score of 2924.0, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances. Single-threaded gzip compression is also strong at 35.4 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is average, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7155.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 9339.42. The processor's support for advanced instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), assists in workloads like small-model LLM inference, where text generation for a 135M model reaches a strong 283.92 tokens/sec.

A notable tradeoff is the memory subsystem's performance under large workloads. While small-block cached memory read bandwidth is average at 691.79 GB/sec, large-block uncached read bandwidth drops to a weak 39.24 GB/sec, reflected in a weak Passmark memory score of 1720.0. Qualitatively, the instance offers a high resource density of memory and local NVMe storage relative to its 8 vCPUs, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring significant memory capacity and fast local scratch space without the overhead of higher vCPU counts.

This server is configured for memory-intensive applications, database operations, text processing pipelines, and light machine learning inference. The combination of 62 GB of RAM and a 402 GB local NVMe SSD supports local caching, software compilation, and medium-scale web serving.
